theme: AI & Robotics: Neural Networks, Humanoids & Automation
title: AI & Robotics: Neural Networks, Humanoids & Automation
description: Comprehensive 60-question assessment exploring the Dartmouth workshop, neural network milestones, chess and Go triumphs, computer vision, and robotics history.

questions.question: At which 1956 summer research workshop at Dartmouth College was the formal term Artificial Intelligence first coined by computer scientist John McCarthy?
questions.explanation: Organized by John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester, and Claude Shannon, the workshop founded AI as an academic discipline.

questions.question: In his landmark 1950 paper Computing Machinery and Intelligence, which British mathematician proposed the Imitation Game test of machine intelligence?
questions.explanation: The Turing Test assesses whether a human interrogator can distinguish conversational text responses of a machine from those of a human.

questions.question: Which 1956 computer program, written by Allen Newell, Herbert Simon, and Cliff Shaw, proved mathematical theorems and is celebrated as the first AI program?
questions.explanation: Logic Theorist proved thirty-eight of the first fifty-two theorems in Whitehead and Russell Principia Mathematica using heuristic search.

questions.question: Which early 1966 natural language processing chatbot created by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT simulated a Rogerian psychotherapist?
questions.explanation: ELIZA used pattern-matching and script substitution to reflect user statements as questions, creating the illusion of understanding.

questions.question: Which 1970s Stanford expert system used a rule-based knowledge engine of 600 rules to identify bacterial blood infections and recommend antibiotics?
questions.explanation: MYCIN demonstrated that symbolic rule-based systems could rival human clinical specialists in narrow diagnostic domains.

questions.question: In what year was the historic Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence convened in New Hampshire?
questions.explanation: The Dartmouth workshop was held in July and August 1956, initiating the modern field of artificial intelligence.

questions.question: Which American psychologist invented the Perceptron in 1958 at Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory, creating the earliest electronic neural network model?
questions.explanation: Rosenblatt Mark I Perceptron used optical photo-cells and motorized potentiometers to learn pattern recognition.

questions.question: Which 1969 book by Marvin Minsky and Seymour Papert proved that single-layer perceptrons could not compute the exclusive-or function, triggering the first AI Winter?
questions.explanation: The mathematical proof that single-layer networks could not solve non-linear XOR problems caused government funding for neural networks to evaporate for a decade.

questions.question: Which foundational learning algorithm for training multi-layer neural networks was popularized in a landmark 1986 Nature paper by Rumelhart, Hinton, and Williams?
questions.explanation: Backpropagation efficiently calculates the gradient of the loss function using the calculus chain rule to update synaptic weights.

questions.question: Which recurrent artificial neural network model, invented by physicist John Hopfield in 1982, serves as an associative content-addressable memory system?
questions.explanation: Hopfield networks guaranteed convergence to local energy minima, bridging statistical physics and computational neuroscience.

questions.question: What non-linear mathematical function, such as ReLU or Sigmoid, is applied to a neuron weighted sum to determine whether it should fire?
questions.explanation: Activation functions introduce non-linearity into neural networks, enabling them to approximate complex multi-dimensional mathematical relationships.

questions.question: In what year did David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton, and Ronald Williams publish their seminal Nature paper on the backpropagation algorithm?
questions.explanation: The landmark paper Learning representations by back-propagating errors was published in Nature on October 9, 1986.

questions.question: In May 1997, which IBM supercomputer made history by becoming the first computer system to defeat a reigning world chess champion in a standard match?
questions.explanation: Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov 3.5 to 2.5 in a six-game rematch in New York using custom chess VLSI chips evaluating 200 million positions per second.

questions.question: In March 2016, which Google DeepMind AI program defeated legendary 18-time world Go champion Lee Sedol in Seoul, South Korea?
questions.explanation: AlphaGo combined deep convolutional policy networks with Monte Carlo Tree Search, famously playing creative Move 37 in Game Two.

questions.question: Which IBM question-answering computer system defeated legendary champions Ken Jennings and Brad Rutter on the quiz show Jeopardy in February 2011?
questions.explanation: Watson analyzed natural language clues, evaluated evidence across four terabytes of structured text, and buzzed in using a robotic finger.

questions.question: Which reinforcement learning backgammon program, developed by Gerald Tesauro at IBM in 1992, played at near-master level through self-play?
questions.explanation: TD-Gammon used temporal difference learning to train a neural network without human expert rules, discovering novel opening strategies.

questions.question: Which DeepMind system mastered chess, shogi, and Go entirely from scratch in just twenty-four hours using pure reinforcement learning without any human games?
questions.explanation: AlphaZero learned exclusively by playing millions of games against itself from raw board rules, convincingly defeating champion engines Stockfish and Elmo.

questions.question: In what year did IBM Deep Blue defeat world chess champion Garry Kasparov in their historic six-game match in New York City?
questions.explanation: Deep Blue defeated Garry Kasparov on May 11, 1997, marking a monumental milestone in artificial intelligence history.

questions.question: Which French computer scientist developed the pioneering LeNet-5 convolutional neural network in 1998, reading handwritten zip codes on checks?
questions.explanation: Yann LeCun utilized spatial weight sharing, convolutional filters, and subsampling pooling layers to recognize characters.

questions.question: Which massive visual database of over fourteen million annotated images, organized by Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li in 2009, accelerated modern deep vision?
questions.explanation: The annual ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge served as the global benchmark proving ground for modern deep neural network architectures.

questions.question: Which deep convolutional network architecture, developed by Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, crushed the 2012 ImageNet challenge?
questions.explanation: AlexNet utilized twin Nvidia GPUs, ReLU non-linearities, and dropout regularization, slashing image classification error rates from twenty-six to fifteen percent.

questions.question: Which 152-layer deep neural network architecture introduced skip residual connections in 2015, solving the vanishing gradient problem in ultra-deep models?
questions.explanation: Invented by Kaiming He and Microsoft researchers, ResNet enabled networks over one hundred layers deep to surpass human visual accuracy.

questions.question: Which popular real-time object detection algorithm, created by Joseph Redmon in 2015, frames object detection as a single regression problem from full image pixels?
questions.explanation: YOLO, short for You Only Look Once, processes images in a single evaluation pass, enabling high-frame-rate real-time video object detection.

questions.question: In what year did AlexNet win the ImageNet competition, widely cited as the catalyst for the modern deep learning boom?
questions.explanation: AlexNet won the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge in September 2012 by an astonishing 10.8 percentage point margin.

questions.question: Which breakthrough 2017 research paper by Google Brain and Google Research introduced the Transformer architecture based purely on self-attention?
questions.explanation: Authors Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, and team replaced recurrent networks with parallel multi-head self-attention mechanisms.

questions.question: What attention mechanism in transformers enables the model to weigh the contextual importance of all other words in a sentence when encoding a given word?
questions.explanation: Self-attention computes query, key, and value dot products across token sequences, capturing distant semantic dependencies across paragraphs.

questions.question: Which Google 2018 natural language model used bidirectional transformer encoders to pre-train deep contextualized representations on unlabeled text?
questions.explanation: BERT, short for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, set state-of-the-art records across eleven major NLP benchmarks.

questions.question: Which 2013 technique developed by Tomas Mikolov at Google mapped words into continuous multi-dimensional vector spaces where semantic relationships are algebraic?
questions.explanation: Word2Vec famously captured semantic analogies in vector space, such as vector King minus vector Man plus vector Woman equaling vector Queen.

questions.question: What generative artificial intelligence model family uses autoregressive transformer decoders pre-trained on internet-scale text to generate coherent human text?
questions.explanation: Generative Pre-trained Transformers predict next-token probabilities sequentially across context windows, demonstrating few-shot learning.

questions.question: In what year was the foundational Attention Is All You Need paper published by Google researchers at NeurIPS?
questions.explanation: The Transformer architecture was published in December 2017, becoming the architectural foundation for all modern large language models.

questions.question: Which two American inventors created the Unimate, the world first industrial robotic arm installed at a General Motors factory in 1961?
questions.explanation: Devol patented the programmable robotic transfer mechanism, while Engelberger founded Unimation, earning the title Father of Robotics.

questions.question: Which pioneering mobile robot developed at Stanford Research Institute from 1966 to 1972 was the first robot to integrate vision, navigation, and problem-solving?
questions.explanation: Shakey used the A-star search algorithm, Hough transforms, and the STRIPS automated planner to navigate rooms and push blocks.

questions.question: Which all-electric six-axis articulated robotic arm, designed by Victor Scheinman at Stanford in 1969, established the kinematic design of modern industrial robots?
questions.explanation: The Stanford Arm featured six rotary joints driven by electric DC motors, allowing computer control of dexterous assembly tasks.

questions.question: Which popular assembly robot design, invented by Hiroshi Makino in 1978, features rigid vertical motion with selective horizontal joint compliance?
questions.explanation: Selective Compliance Assembly Robot Arms are widely used in high-speed electronics assembly for precise pick-and-place insertion.

questions.question: Which legendary science fiction author formulated the famous Three Laws of Robotics in his 1942 short story Runaround?
questions.explanation: Asimov laws dictated that a robot may not injure a human, must obey human orders, and must protect its own existence unless in conflict with the first two laws.

questions.question: In what year was the first Unimate industrial robotic arm deployed on an active assembly line at General Motors in Ewing, New Jersey?
questions.explanation: The hydraulic Unimate arm was installed in 1961 to lift red-hot die-cast door handles and weld them onto auto bodies.

questions.question: Which iconic white humanoid robot was introduced by Honda in 2000, capable of fluid walking, running, climbing stairs, and greeting dignitaries?
questions.explanation: ASIMO, short for Advanced Step in Innovative Mobility, pioneered Zero Moment Point dynamic trajectory balancing during bipedal gait.

questions.question: Which Massachusetts engineering robotics company developed the Atlas bipedal humanoid robot and the four-legged Spot quadruped robot?
questions.explanation: Founded by Marc Raibert as an MIT spinoff, Boston Dynamics achieved breakthroughs in real-time dynamic balance, parkour, and hydraulic control.

questions.question: What 1973 robotic project at Waseda University in Japan was the world first full-scale anthropomorphic humanoid robot with limb control and vision?
questions.explanation: WABOT-1 had artificial ears, mouth, and eyes, able to converse in Japanese and walk slowly with two artificial legs.

questions.question: What bipedal walking principle, pioneered by Miomir Vukobratović, ensures that dynamic ground reaction forces prevent a robot from tipping over?
questions.explanation: ZMP balance algorithms ensure that the net horizontal inertia and gravity moments around the contact support polygon equal zero.

questions.question: What robotic quadruped created by Boston Dynamics for DARPA in 2005 was nicknamed BigDog for carrying heavy military loads across rough terrain?
questions.explanation: BigDog utilized a small go-kart engine and hydraulic actuators, famously recovering its footing on ice when kicked.

questions.question: In what year did Honda officially introduce the ASIMO humanoid robot to the public in Tokyo?
questions.explanation: Honda unveiled ASIMO on November 20, 2000, following fourteen years of secret bipedal humanoid robotics research.

questions.question: Which microwave-oven-sized robotic rover deployed by NASA Mars Pathfinder on July 4, 1997, was the first wheeled vehicle on Mars?
questions.explanation: Sojourner operated for eighty-three days on the Martian surface, using a rocker-bogie suspension to analyze rock compositions.

questions.question: Which one-ton car-sized NASA rover landed in Mars Gale Crater in August 2012 using an audacious rocket-powered sky crane descent stage?
questions.explanation: Curiosity discovered chemical evidence of ancient habitable freshwater lakes and organic carbon molecules on early Mars.

questions.question: What small robotic coaxial helicopter deployed by NASA Perseverance rover achieved the first powered controlled flight on another planet in 2021?
questions.explanation: Ingenuity completed seventy-two successful flights through the thin Martian atmosphere over nearly three years of operations.

questions.question: Which 2005 autonomous vehicle competition organized by DARPA was won by Stanford University robotic Volkswagen Touareg named Stanley?
questions.explanation: Led by Sebastian Thrun, Stanley navigated 212 kilometers of rugged Mojave Desert terrain in under seven hours with zero human intervention.

questions.question: What optical remote sensing sensor uses pulsed laser beams to generate precise three-dimensional point clouds of surrounding environments for self-driving cars?
questions.explanation: Light Detection and Ranging measures the time-of-flight of millions of laser reflections per second to create high-definition 3D maps.

questions.question: In what year did Stanford autonomous car Stanley win the historic DARPA Grand Challenge across the Mojave Desert?
questions.explanation: Stanley won the DARPA Grand Challenge on October 8, 2005, claiming the two-million-dollar prize and igniting the modern autonomous vehicle industry.

questions.question: In machine learning, what framework models an autonomous agent making sequential decisions by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative reward?
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning optimizes policy functions through trial and error, balancing exploration of new strategies with exploitation of known rewards.

questions.question: Which mathematical framework forms the formal foundation for reinforcement learning, defined by states, actions, transition probabilities, and rewards?
questions.explanation: MDPs assume the Markov property, where future states depend solely on the current state and action rather than historical paths.

questions.question: Which model-free reinforcement learning algorithm developed by Chris Watkins in 1989 learns the expected utility of taking a given action in a given state?
questions.explanation: Q-learning iteratively updates a table or network of Q-values using the Bellman equation to derive optimal action-selection policies.

questions.question: Which DeepMind system published in Nature in 2015 learned to play forty-nine Atari 2600 video games at super-human levels using raw pixels as input?
questions.explanation: DQN combined Q-learning with deep convolutional neural networks and experience replay memory buffers to achieve stable training.

questions.question: Which OpenAI system comprising five neural networks defeated world champion esports team OG in the complex video game Dota 2 in 2019?
questions.explanation: OpenAI Five played tens of thousands of years of simulated game experience each day using scaled proximal policy optimization algorithms.

questions.question: In what year did DeepMind publish its landmark Nature paper Human-level control through deep reinforcement learning demonstrating DQN on Atari?
questions.explanation: DeepMind published the historic paper on February 26, 2015, featured on the cover of Nature.

questions.question: What counterintuitive observation in AI states that high-level abstract reasoning is easy for computers, while low-level sensory-motor skills are extremely difficult?
questions.explanation: Hans Moravec noted that a four-year-old child easily perceives faces and walks across a room, skills that require enormous engineering for robots.

questions.question: What statistical problem occurs when a machine learning model fits training data too closely, capturing random noise and failing to generalize to new data?
questions.explanation: Overfitting is mitigated using techniques such as dropout, weight decay L2 regularization, cross-validation, and larger training datasets.

questions.question: What phenomenon describes when a generative large language model produces convincing, authoritative-sounding text that is completely factually false?
questions.explanation: Hallucinations occur because probabilistic language models generate statistically likely next tokens without explicit internal ground-truth verification.

questions.question: What generative model architecture generates high-fidelity images by learning to reverse a gradual process of adding Gaussian noise to training images?
questions.explanation: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models underpin modern image generators such as Stable Diffusion, Midjourney, and DALL-E.

questions.question: What AI safety challenge seeks to ensure that artificial intelligence systems reliably adhere to human intentions, values, and ethical principles?
questions.explanation: Alignment research uses methods like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback to prevent models from exhibiting deceptive or harmful behaviors.

questions.question: In what year did Alan Turing publish Computing Machinery and Intelligence introducing the Imitation Game test in the philosophical journal Mind?
questions.explanation: Alan Turing published his seminal paper in October 1950, opening with the famous question: Can machines think?
